- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–4% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model often overreacts; reduce forecast slope or apply downward bias of 1–2% per day.
- When true price drops below 75 after a peak, model frequently fails to recognize mean reversion; apply a 2–5% downward correction if price is below 75 for 2+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values or reduce volatility by 10–20%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early days (1–7) when sentiment is rising; reduce first 3–5 days by 1–2% if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast if sentiment <0.27 and price <75.
- When sentiment is high and price is falling, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast if sentiment >0.77 and price is falling.
